questions.stem: Why is cracking carried out on long-chain hydrocarbons?

options.text: To convert excess long-chain fractions into shorter, more useful alkanes and alkenes
To make them safer to transport
To remove sulfur impurities from the fractions
To change them from liquids to gases for storage

questions.explanation: Fractional distillation produces more long-chain hydrocarbons than needed, but there is high demand for shorter molecules like petrol. Cracking breaks long chains into shorter, more useful alkanes (fuels) and alkenes (for making polymers and other chemicals).
